i.norm: Encodes an ASCII string as UTF-16LE, then decodes the resulting bytes as UTF-8. In UTF-16LE every ASCII character is stored as its low byte followed by a zero (high) byte. When those same bytes are read back as UTF-8, each pair decodes to the original character followed by a U+0000 (NUL) character, so the round-trip deliberately does NOT reproduce the original string: the result is the input with a NUL inserted after every character (including a trailing NUL after the final 'W').
Expected = each input character followed by the NUL that came from the UTF-16LE high byte.
